key_insight: MgHCu3 remains structurally and electronically robust, but its phonons and predicted superconducting Tc are highly sensitive to computational settings, lowering confidence in the originally claimed 42 K superconductivity.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that claimed high-Tc hydride/perovskite superconductivity must be validated with multiple functionals and dense sampling before being used as a design target or screening result.
method: Revisited MgHCu3 with PBEsol and PBE DFT functionals
Compared crystal/electronic structure against k-point and functional choices
Recomputed lattice dynamics, phonon dispersion, electron-phonon coupling, and Tc under different Gaussian broadenings
evidence_signal: Computed Tc values varied widely, from about 10 K to 31 K depending on broadening, and did not exceed the classical 40 K limit.
watch_item: Phonon-related predictions are extremely grid- and functional-dependent, so single-method DFT claims of high Tc may be unreliable without cross-checks and experiment.
